statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n integers naming the fruit type on each tree in a row. You pick one fruit per tree while walking a contiguous stretch, carrying two baskets, each holding a single type. Print the longest stretch you can fully pick: the longest window containing at most two distinct values. Grow the right end, keep per-type counts, and while a third type is inside, shrink from the left - a type leaves only when its count reaches zero.

example.why: From the second tree the types are 1, 2, 2 - two kinds; all four trees would need three baskets.

hint: Track a live distinct counter; it falls only on a zero-crossing of some type's count.
mistake: Remembering just the last two types seen instead of counts - the window forgets how many of each remain.
